items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: And I called Jamal, who I did not know at all at that time, and told him what I was doing and asked if he’d like to participate and he said sure.

ctx.x: capable of being influenced simultaneously by Horace Silver and Lennie Tristano. You try that sometime and you know what you get? You get Bill Evans. And the other fact is that yes, I was tremendously impressed by Bill and the interesting thing about Bill of course was that in an age when then, as is true now I’m quite sure, of course it is, guys will kill to get into the recording studio. Everybody is always ready and more than ready to record. After Bill did that first record which got very, very good critical…

Ahmad Jamal feeling positive about Bill Evans. Well the nice thing see about going out after those quotes, it so happens I got four quotes out of four people. But if it had taken eight or ten people to come up with the four good quotes nobody would have known that when the record came out. But those were the only four people, and as I say Miles’ quote was in existence. Getting a quote from him might have been another whole thing but I didn’t have to. I just would say Miles I’m going to use this, okay? And I…

anniversary of that recording, I got a call from a New Yorker writer, Adam Gopnick. I was interviewed, Paul was interviewed, Lorraine Gordon, who incidentally is the woman who I obliquely referred to under her first married name, the woman who was originally married to Alfred Lion at Blue Note ended up being married to the widower and now, for a number of years the owner of the Village Vanguard. So Lorraine was the best they could do in terms of dealing with the Vanguard thing. So I got to be quoted in the New…
